d01.title: Set up your real repo
d01.why: The 30 days happen in your own repo, not the starter. Day one is the ground floor.
d01.done: CLAUDE.md is committed and under 60 lines.

items.text: In your own repo run `claude`, then `/init`. Trim the generated CLAUDE.md to under 60 lines using cards/CLAUDE.md.template.
cards/command-card.md, the 8 daily commands section.
One line: "Day 1: CLAUDE.md in <repo>, N lines."

d02.title: Plan one small ticket
d02.why: Plan mode is the habit that makes everything else cheap.
d02.done: plans/d02.md exists and you could hand it to a teammate.

items.text: cards/prompt-ingredients.md
Pick your smallest open ticket. Shift+Tab into plan mode, brief Claude with the 5 ingredients, save the plan as plans/d02.md in your repo. Do not build yet.
The Task line of your brief, one sentence.

d03.title: Second repo
d03.why: One repo is a trial. Two repos is a habit.
d03.done: Two repos have a CLAUDE.md, two plans saved.

items.text: Run `/init` in a second repo (a side project counts). Trim it the same way as day 1.
Plan mode on one ticket there. Save the plan as plans/d03.md.
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory

d04.title: Two briefs, two plans
d04.why: The brief is the skill. The plan is how you check it.
d04.done: Four plans saved so far this week (d02, d03, d04-a, d04-b).

items.text: Write a 5-ingredient brief for two small tasks, one per repo. Run plan mode on each, save plans/d04-a.md and plans/d04-b.md.
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows
One thing a plan surprised you with.

d05.title: Ship it via plan mode
d05.why: Friday outcome: one feature shipped through a plan you approved.
d05.done: PR open, tests green, five plans in plans/.

items.text: Take the d02 plan. Approve it, let Claude build, run the tests yourself, commit on a branch, open the PR. Save the final plan as plans/d05.md.
Friday screenshot of `node mw.js status` plus the PR link.

d06.title: The loop, day one
d06.why: Plan, build, test, commit. Once a day until it is boring.
d06.done: One commit with tests, message edited by you.

items.text: One small feature: plan mode, approve, build. Run `! npm test` (or your test command) yourself before you accept the result.
Ask Claude for the commit message. Edit it in your own words, then commit.
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode

d07.title: Test first
d07.why: A test written before the code is a brief Claude cannot misread.
d07.done: The test commit lands before the code commit.

items.text: `/clear`. Write the test for today's feature first, commit it, then ask Claude to make it pass.
Commit message: Claude writes, you edit.
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs

d08.title: Watch the context
d08.why: Context is the budget. Learn to see it.
d08.done: Feature committed, and you used /compact with an instruction once.

items.text: Feature three. Half way through, run `/context` and look at what is big.
`/compact` with an instruction naming what to keep, then finish the feature and commit.
One line: what was eating your context.

d09.title: Clear between tasks
d09.why: Old context makes new work worse and costs more on every message.

items.text: Two unrelated tasks today: a feature and a bug fix. `/clear` between them. Notice the quality of the second answer.
cards/command-card.md, the 8 rules for a full day on the Pro plan.

d10.title: Five features, five tests
d10.why: Friday outcome: one small feature a day, a test on each, messages you can read in a year.
d10.done: Five feature commits this week, each with a test.

items.text: Feature five. Then read your five commit messages with `git log --oneline -5` and reword any that do not say why.
Friday screenshot of `node mw.js status` plus "5 features, N tests".

d11.title: Use the checklist
d11.why: AI code looks right. The checklist finds where it is not.
d11.done: Checklist run on one real diff, by hand.

items.text: cards/review-checklist.md
Run the 10 questions on yesterday's diff by hand. Note which ones you could not answer in a minute.
One line: which question caught something, or "all clear".

d12.title: Claude reviews Claude
d12.why: A fresh session with no memory of writing the code is an honest reviewer.
d12.done: One review saved, the checklist in your PR template.

items.text: `/clear`. Paste the checklist and ask Claude to review today's diff against it. Save the output as reviews/d12.md.
Add the 10 questions to your PR template (.github/pull_request_template.md or your team's equivalent).
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide

d13.title: Hook one: tests before commit
d13.why: A hook is a rule that does not depend on anyone remembering.

items.text: Add a git pre-commit hook in your repo that runs the tests and blocks the commit when red. Break a test on purpose and try to commit, to prove it.
Claude reviews Claude on today's diff. Save reviews/d13.md.
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

d14.title: Hook two: inside Claude Code
d14.why: The second hook runs inside Claude Code, on every edit it makes.

items.text: In .claude/settings.json add a PostToolUse hook that runs your formatter or linter after Claude edits a file. Make one edit and watch it run.
Claude reviews Claude on today's diff. Save reviews/d14.md.
One line: what your two hooks do.

d15.title: Security pass
d15.why: Friday outcome: checklist on every PR, two hooks, one review a day.
d15.done: Security review run, one finding handled.

items.text: Run `/security-review` on this week's branch. Fix one finding, or write down why it is a false positive.
Claude reviews Claude on today's diff. Save reviews/d15.md.
Friday screenshot of `node mw.js status` plus "2 hooks, N reviews".

d16.title: Your leverage map
d16.why: Leverage starts with knowing which chore to kill first.

items.text: cards/leverage-map.md
Fill the five-row chore table. Pick the top row and write a one-line brief for it.
One line: the chore you picked and its hours per week.

d17.title: Write a skill
d17.why: A skill is a prompt you never retype.

items.text: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
Create .claude/skills/<chore>/SKILL.md for yesterday's chore. Run it as /<chore> on a real case. Fix the prompt once.

d18.title: A subagent with one job
d18.why: A subagent has its own context and its own instructions. It does one thing well.
d18.done: Subagent used once on real work.

items.text: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents
Write .claude/agents/<name>.md for one job (test writer, doc checker, migration reviewer). Use it on one task today.
One line: what your subagent does.

d19.title: MCP on real data
d19.why: MCP lets Claude read your real data instead of your description of it.
d19.done: Claude answered one real data question through MCP.

items.text: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp
Connect one real data source by MCP (a database, GitHub, Jira, or your logs). Ask one question you would normally answer by hand. Save the answer as notes/d19.md.

d20.title: All three on one ticket
d20.why: Friday outcome: a skill, a subagent and an MCP source, all used on real work.
d20.done: Ticket done, CLAUDE.md names your three levers.

items.text: Take one real ticket. Use your skill, your subagent and your MCP source on it. Point to each from CLAUDE.md in one line.
Friday screenshot of `node mw.js status` plus your three levers in one line.

d21.title: Pick the tool
d21.why: A small tool your team uses beats a big one nobody finishes.

items.text: Pick one internal tool your team needs (a report, a cleanup script, a small dashboard, a bot). Write a 5-ingredient brief for it as TOOL.md.
cards/prompt-ingredients.md
One line: the tool and who will use it.

d22.title: Build v1
d22.why: Version one is the smallest thing a teammate can run.
d22.done: v1 runs on your machine with tests green.

items.text: Plan mode on TOOL.md. Approve, build v1, write tests, commit on a branch.
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings

d23.title: A teammate runs it
d23.why: It is not shipped until someone else has run it.
d23.done: One teammate has run it and their one issue is fixed.

items.text: Write the README run steps. Ask one teammate to run it and tell you one thing that broke or confused them. Fix that one thing.
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions
One line: what the teammate said.

d24.title: Make it run itself
d24.why: A tool that runs on its own saves the hours you are about to promise.
d24.done: CI green, script rehearsed with real numbers.

items.text: Add CI (GitHub Actions running your tests) or a schedule, whichever the tool needs. Push and watch it go green.
cards/manager-script.md
Rehearse the 3-line script out loud with your three numbers filled in.

d25.title: Demo to your manager
d25.why: Friday outcome: built end to end, shown to the person who asked you to use AI.
d25.done: Demo done, three numbers said out loud.

items.text: Demo the internal tool to your manager using cards/manager-script.md. Bring the three numbers.
Friday screenshot of `node mw.js status` plus the one line your manager said back.

d26.title: Teach one teammate
d26.why: Teaching is how the habit survives a busy week.
d26.done: A teammate ran /init and saved a plan.

items.text: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart
Pair with one teammate for 20 minutes. They drive: `/init` on their repo, one plan in plan mode. You only point.
One line: who you taught and what they planned.

d27.title: Team rules
d27.why: A team CLAUDE.md makes every engineer's Claude follow the same conventions.
d27.done: PR open for team rules, one reviewer asked.

items.text: Open a PR with a team CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/ files for a shared repo. Keep it under 60 lines. Ask for one review.
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory

d28.title: Write the update, book the call
d28.why: Written updates travel further than demos.

items.text: Send the 5-line written update from cards/manager-script.md to your manager or team channel.
One line: "Booking the follow-up Q&A call" with your preferred slot.
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security

d29.title: Draft your own command card
d29.why: The commands you actually used are the ones worth keeping.
d29.done: A draft card with 8 commands and one line each.

items.text: From `/resume` and your shell history, list the 8 commands you used most in 30 days. Write one line each: when to use it.
cards/command-card.md

d30.title: Post your card
d30.why: Day 30: you wrote the card you were handed on day one.

items.text: Write your own command card (8 commands, 8 rules that worked for you) as my-command-card.md and commit it to your repo.
Post your command card in the group.
Final `node mw.js status` screenshot with one line: what changed in how you work.
